mainTopic: רבי שמעון's chain of קל וחומר on 'לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך', its refutations, רבא's praise, and whether a prohibition can come from a קל וחומר
overview: This amud opens with the end of רבי שמעון's statement: since the other items in the פסוק 'לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך' can be learned by קל וחומר, the פסוק teaches that someone who eats an עולה after זריקה is flogged, even inside the עזרה. רבא praises רבי שמעון very highly, but admits that each of his קל וחומר arguments can be refuted. The גמרא then goes through the whole chain: בכורים, מעשר, תודה and שלמים, בכור, חטאת and אשם, and עולה. Each time it answers 'אדרבה' and shows that the supposedly lighter item is stricter in some other way. It ends by noting that every item is stricter than an עולה, because each has two eatings. So what was רבא praising? The answer is רבי שמעון's skill in rearranging the פסוק to reach his view. The גמרא next objects that a prohibition cannot be learned from a קל וחומר (אין מזהירין מן הדין), and answers that רבי שמעון derives only a general איסור. It then challenges that answer from רבא's ruling of five sets of lashes and from the משנה 'אלו הן הלוקין'. The answer to that last challenge comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The real lesson of the verse: eating a burnt-offering after sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון concludes that the פסוק is needed only to teach that eating an עולה after זריקה earns lashes, even inside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse comes only to teach about someone who eats from a burnt-offering after the blood was sprinkled, even inside the courtyard, that he is flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of רבי שמעון's statement. Since the other items in the פסוק can be learned by קל וחומר, he says the פסוק itself is really teaching one new law about the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is burned completely on the מזבח, so nobody may eat its meat at all. רבי שמעון says that eating it after זריקה earns מלקות even inside the עזרה. That is a new law that a קל וחומר could not have taught, so the פסוק is needed for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח
Sprinkling the blood of a קרבן on the מזבח
Inside the courtyard of the בית המקדש
Receives lashes (מלקות)

phrases.english: Rather, to teach about one who eats from the burnt-offering
after the sprinkling, even inside,
that he is flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends רבי שמעון's chain of קל וחומר arguments from the earlier part of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who eats the meat of an עולה after זריקה, even inside the עזרה, receives מלקות.

steps.title: רבא's praise of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבא praises רבי שמעון: a mother should give birth only to a child like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If a woman's child will be like רבי שמעון, let her give birth; and if not, let her not give birth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is so impressed by רבי שמעון's careful reasoning that he holds him up as the model of what a child should become.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is praise, not a legal ruling. רבא admires how רבי שמעון could explain the whole פסוק by building a chain of logical arguments.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives birth
His mother
Let her give birth

phrases.english: Rava said:
One whose mother bears a child like Rabbi Shimon, let her bear,
and if not, let her not bear.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: דְּיָלְידָא אִימֵּיהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבי שמעון's derivation with praise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא praises רבי שמעון as the model of a wise man.

steps.title: רבא admits the arguments can be refuted
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that he praises רבי שמעון even though each of his קל וחומר arguments has a refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is so even though they have a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבא says the arguments are open to refutation, and the גמרא will now show what those refutations are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר works only if one item is stricter than the other in every way. A פירכא points out a way the supposedly lighter item is actually stricter, and that breaks the argument. רבא is admitting that each step of רבי שמעון's chain has a weak spot like this.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation of a קל וחומר, showing the 'lighter' item is stricter in some way
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not taking back his praise. He admires the brilliance of the reasoning even though the arguments can technically be refuted.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא.
phrases.english: And even though they have a refutation.
phrases.notes: "They" means each of רבי שמעון's קל וחומר arguments.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the praise in step 2 and opens a review of refutations.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's chain of קל וחומר arguments
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each קל וחומר can be broken by showing the 'lighter' item is stricter in some other way.

steps.title: Why first fruits seem stricter than tithe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the basis of the first קל וחומר: בכורים are forbidden to non-כהנים, while מעשר שני is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the stringency of first fruits over tithe? That they are forbidden to non-priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the stringency that made בכורים seem stricter than מעשר שני. That is the base of the קל וחומר it is about to refute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reasoned from מעשר שני to בכורים: if the lighter מעשר may not be eaten outside ירושלים, then the stricter בכורים surely may not. The reason בכורים seem stricter is that only כהנים may eat them, while anyone may eat מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Stringency; what makes something stricter
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש and given to a כהן
Here, מעשר שני: tithe eaten by its owner in ירושלים
Non-כהנים

phrases.english: What is the stringency of first fruits over tithe?
That they are forbidden to non-priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts showing the refutations that רבא mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What stringency of בכורים made the קל וחומר from מעשר work?

steps.title: Refutation: tithe is forbidden to a mourner
steps.stepSummary: On the contrary, מעשר is stricter in one way, because an אונן may not eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, tithe is stricter, since it is forbidden to an acute mourner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא breaks the first קל וחומר by showing a way that מעשר is actually stricter than בכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אונן is a person whose close relative died that day, and he may not eat מעשר שני. According to רבי שמעון, an אונן may eat בכורים. So each item is stricter in a different way, and you cannot reason from מעשר to בכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
A mourner on the day a close relative died
Stricter

phrases.english: On the contrary, tithe is stricter,
since it is forbidden to an acute mourner.
phrases.notes: See דברים 26:14, where the owner declares that he did not eat מעשר while he was a mourner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, מַעֲשֵׂר חָמוּר, שֶׁכֵּן אָסוּר לְאוֹנֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the stringency named in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from מעשר to בכורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר has its own stringency, since an אונן may not eat it, so it is not simply the lighter item.

steps.title: Why thanks- and peace-offerings seem stricter than tithe
steps.stepSummary: The basis of the next קל וחומר: תודה and שלמים need their blood and parts placed on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the stringency of a thanks-offering and peace-offering over tithe? That they require placement of blood and sacrificial parts on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the stringency behind the next step of רבי שמעון's chain, so that it can refute it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reasoned that תודה and שלמים are stricter than מעשר שני because they are real קרבנות whose blood and אימורים go on the מזבח. מעשר has nothing like that.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks-offering
Peace-offering
Placing the blood on the מזבח
The fat parts of a קרבן burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: And what is the stringency of a thanks-offering and peace-offering over tithe?
That they require placement of blood
and sacrificial parts upon the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next link in רבי שמעון's chain, following the same pattern as step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What stringency of תודה and שלמים made the קל וחומר from מעשר work?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They need מתן דמים and אימורים on the מזבח.

steps.title: Refutation: tithe needs minted coins for redemption
steps.stepSummary: On the contrary, מעשר is stricter in one way, because it can only be redeemed with minted coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, tithe is stricter, since it requires minted money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא breaks the second קל וחומר by showing a way that מעשר is stricter than תודה and שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני may be redeemed only with a coin that has a stamped image. A disqualified קרבן may be redeemed with any item of the same value. So מעשר is stricter here, and the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Money with a stamped image; a minted coin
Require

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern: each קל וחומר of רבי שמעון rests on one stringency, and the גמרא answers with 'אדרבה', pointing to a different way the supposedly lighter item is stricter. That is what רבא meant by 'they have a פירכא'.

phrases.english: On the contrary, tithe is stricter,
since it requires minted money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, מַעֲשֵׂר חָמוּר, שֶׁכֵּן טְעוּנִין כֶּסֶף צוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the stringency named in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from מעשר to תודה and שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר is stricter because it can be redeemed only with minted coins, while a קרבן can be redeemed with anything of equal value.

steps.title: Why a firstborn is stricter than thanks and peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the basis of the next קל וחומר: a בכור is holy from the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes a בכור stricter than a תודה and שלמים? Its holiness starts from the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next link in the chain and asks why a בכור counts as stricter than תודה and שלמים. It answers that a בכור is holy from the moment it is born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה or שלמים becomes holy only when its owner sets it aside as a קרבן. A בכור is holy automatically from birth, with no one needing to set it aside. This is the stringency the קל וחומר leans on.

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency; a way in which something is stricter
A firstborn kosher animal, which is given to a כהן and brought as a קרבן
The thanks-offering and the peace-offering, offerings of lesser holiness
Its holiness comes from the womb, meaning it is holy from birth

phrases.english: And what is the stringency of a firstborn
over a thanks-offering and a peace-offering?
That its holiness is from the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same pattern as Steps 4 and 6, now applied to the next link in the chain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes a בכור stricter than תודה and שלמים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בכור is holy from the womb.

steps.title: Thanks and peace offerings are stricter in other ways
steps.stepSummary: On the contrary, תודה and שלמים are stricter: they need סמיכה, נסכים, and waving of the breast and thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, תודה and שלמים are stricter, because they need סמיכה, נסכים, and the waving of the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 8 and shows that תודה and שלמים are stricter in several ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה or שלמים needs three things a בכור does not: placing hands on the animal, wine libations, and waving the breast and thigh. So it is not clear that a בכור is the stricter one, and the קל וחומר can be refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; it is the opposite
Leaning one's hands on the animal's head before it is brought
Libations of wine, with flour and oil, brought along with certain קרבנות
Waving the breast and thigh of the animal before they are given to the כהן

phrases.english: On the contrary: a thanks-offering and a peace-offering are stricter,
since they require placing of hands,
and libations, and waving of the breast and thigh.
phrases.notes: A בכור needs none of these three things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the stringency named in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a בכור is stricter than תודה and שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תודה and שלמים have their own stringencies that a בכור lacks, so neither one is clearly stricter, and the קל וחומר breaks down.

steps.title: Why sin and guilt offerings are stricter than a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The basis of the next קל וחומר: חטאת and אשם are קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes חטאת and אשם stricter than a בכור? They are קדשי קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next link and asks why חטאת and אשם are stricter than a בכור. It answers that they belong to the highest level of holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is only קדשים קלים, a lighter level of holiness. חטאת and אשם are קדשי קדשים, the most holy level. That higher rank is the stringency the קל וחומר uses.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin-offering and the guilt-offering
Offerings of the most holy level

phrases.english: And what is the stringency of a sin-offering and a guilt-offering
over a firstborn?
That they are offerings of the most holy level.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern, applied to the next link in the chain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes חטאת and אשם stricter than a בכור?

steps.title: A firstborn is stricter because it is holy from birth
steps.stepSummary: On the contrary, a בכור is stricter, since its holiness comes from the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, a בכור is stricter, because its holiness is from the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 10, using the same point it already raised in Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is holy from birth, while חטאת and אשם become holy only when someone sets them aside. So a בכור has its own stringency, and the קל וחומר can be refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: Stricter; more severe

phrases.english: On the contrary, a firstborn is stricter,
since its holiness is from the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the stringency named in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חטאת and אשם are stricter than a בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בכור has a stringency that חטאת and אשם lack, being holy from birth, so the comparison cannot run in only one direction.

steps.title: Why the burnt offering is stricter than sin and guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: The basis of the last קל וחומר: an עולה is burned completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes an עולה stricter than חטאת and אשם? It is burned entirely on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last link and asks why an עולה is stricter than חטאת and אשם. It answers that an עולה is burned completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Parts of a חטאת or אשם are eaten by the כהנים. An עולה is burned whole on the מזבח, and no one eats from it. That is the stringency behind this קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The burnt-offering
Whole; burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: And what is the stringency of a burnt-offering
over a sin-offering and a guilt-offering? That it is burned whole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern, applied to the last link in the chain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes an עולה stricter than חטאת and אשם?

steps.title: Sin and guilt offerings are stricter because they atone
steps.stepSummary: On the contrary, חטאת and אשם are stricter, since they bring atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, חטאת and אשם are stricter, because they atone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 12 and shows that חטאת and אשם are stricter in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאת and אשם bring atonement for specific sins. That is an important quality, and it can count as more serious than being burned whole. So this קל וחומר can be refuted too.

keyTerms.meaning: They atone; they bring forgiveness for a sin

phrases.english: On the contrary, a sin-offering and a guilt-offering are stricter,
since they atone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the stringency named in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an עולה is stricter than חטאת and אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חטאת and אשם atone for sin, a stringency the עולה lacks, so the עולה is not clearly stricter.

steps.title: Every item in the list is stricter than a burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: All the other items are stricter than an עולה, because each of them is eaten twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them are stricter than an עולה, because they have two eatings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one last, wide-ranging challenge. Every other item in the chain is stricter than an עולה in one shared way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the other items is eaten twice: once by the מזבח and once by people, such as the כהנים or the owners. An עולה is only burned on the מזבח, so it has just one eating. This turns the עולה's special feature into a weakness, so the final link of רבי שמעון's chain is refuted from every side.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them
Two eatings: by the מזבח and by people

steps.whatToRemember: The whole chain of קל וחומר arguments of רבי שמעון can be pushed back at every link with 'on the contrary'. That is why רבא in Step 3 said that each of them has a refutation, even though he praised רבי שמעון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the review of the chain and backs up רבא's claim from Step 3 that every one of these קל וחומר arguments can be refuted.

phrases.english: And all of them are stricter than a burnt-offering,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means every item in the chain: בכורים, מעשר, תודה and שלמים, בכור, חטאת and אשם.

phrases.english: since they have two eatings!
phrases.notes: Part goes on the מזבח and part is eaten by people, while an עולה goes only on the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a broader refutation of the עולה link, applying to every item in the list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The final קל וחומר, which treats עולה as the strictest item
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every other item has two eatings, while the עולה has only one, so all of them are stricter than the עולה in this respect.

steps.title: What was the praise of רבי שמעון about?
steps.stepSummary: Every one of רבי שמעון's קל וחומר arguments was refuted. So what did רבא mean when he praised anyone whose mother bears a child like רבי שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the meaning of the praise: 'whoever's mother bears a child like רבי שמעון'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא praised רבי שמעון so highly, when all of his קל וחומר arguments were just knocked down. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא praised רבי שמעון's derivation in strong terms. But in Steps 4-14, every קל וחומר in the chain was answered with 'on the contrary, that one is stricter.' So the praise now seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, what then? (asks what something really means once the obvious explanation fails)
Whose mother gives birth to him

phrases.english: Rather, what is the meaning of
'whose mother bears a child like רבי שמעון'?
phrases.notes: This refers to רבא's praise back in Step 2: a mother should bear a son like רבי שמעון, or better not bear at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי דְּיָלְידָא אִימֵּיהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the refutations in Steps 4-14 and asks what is left of רבא's praise from Step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What quality of רבי שמעון did רבא praise, if his arguments can all be refuted?

steps.title: The praise is for how he rearranges the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא praised רבי שמעון's skill in rearranging the order of the פסוק so that it leads to the conclusion he holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: To reach what he himself holds, he rearranges the verse and interprets it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא was not praising the strength of the קל וחומר arguments. He was praising רבי שמעון's clever method of reading the פסוק in a new order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון did not read the פסוק from beginning to end. He started from the last item, ביכורים, and worked backward to reach his conclusion. Even if each argument can be refuted, that creative reading is what impressed רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rearranges, reorders (the parts of a פסוק)
What he holds, his opinion

phrases.english: That in order to reach what he himself holds,
he rearranges the verse and interprets it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The praise was for רבי שמעון's skill in reordering the פסוק, not for the strength of each קל וחומר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's praise of רבי שמעון stands even though his arguments were refuted. It is praise for his method of reading the פסוק.

steps.title: You can't learn a warning from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: How could רבי שמעון derive prohibitions from a קל וחומר? Even those who allow punishment based on a קל וחומר agree that a prohibition cannot be derived from one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can one derive a warning from a קל וחומר? Even according to the view that punishes based on a קל וחומר, one does not derive a warning from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole idea behind רבי שמעון's approach. A prohibition (אזהרה) is never learned from a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a person to receive מלקות, the Torah must clearly warn against the act. There is a known debate about whether a punishment can be learned from a קל וחומר. But everyone agrees that the warning itself cannot be learned that way. So how did רבי שמעון create new prohibitions this way?

keyTerms.meaning: We derive a warning (a לאו, a prohibition)
We punish (derive a punishment)
From a logical argument, a קל וחומר
A Torah warning that is needed before someone can be punished

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'עונשין' (deriving a punishment) with 'מזהירין' (deriving the prohibition itself). Some allow the first from a קל וחומר, but nobody allows the second.

phrases.english: And does one derive a prohibition from a קל וחומר?
But even according to the one who says
one punishes based on a קל וחומר,
one does not derive a prohibition from a קל וחומר!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי שמעון's method of reading the פסוק to the legal power of his derivations.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's derivation of prohibitions through קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyone agrees that an אזהרה cannot come from a קל וחומר, so these derivations cannot create prohibitions.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'אין מזהירין מן הדין' is a basic principle about which prohibitions can lead to מלקות.

steps.title: Only a plain prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון only derives a general prohibition, not a לאו that carries מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is merely a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון's קל וחומר only creates a general איסור. It does not create a warning that leads to מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'אין מזהירין מן הדין' applies only to a full לאו that brings מלקות. A lighter, general איסור can still come from a קל וחומר, so רבי שמעון does not break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A mere prohibition (forbidden, but with no מלקות)

phrases.english: It is a mere prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the derived law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון derives full לאוין with מלקות from a קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only derives a general איסור, with no מלקות.

steps.title: רבא says he gets five sets of lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבא ruled that, according to רבי שמעון, a זר who eats an עולה before זריקה outside the walls is לוקה five times. That suggests real מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבא say: a non-כהן who ate from an עולה before the blood was sprinkled, outside the wall, is לוקה five times according to רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 18 with רבא's ruling. That ruling says רבי שמעון gives actual lashes for these prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five come from five things: being a זר, eating an עולה, eating before זריקה, eating קדשי קדשים outside the עזרה, and eating קדשים outside ירושלים. If רבי שמעון gives five sets of מלקות, these must be real לאוין and not just general prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן
Sprinkling the blood of a קרבן on the מזבח
Outside the wall (of the Temple courtyard or of ירושלים)
Receives מלקות (lashes)

phrases.english: But didn't רבא say:
A non-כהן who ate from a burnt-offering
before the sprinkling, outside the wall,
according to רבי שמעון is flogged five times!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer 'איסורא בעלמא' from Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון derives only general prohibitions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא said 'לוקה', which means real lashes, so these must be full לאוין.

steps.title: It means five prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רבא's 'לוקה חמש' really means that the person has violated five prohibitions, not that he gets five sets of lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are five prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reinterprets רבא's words. 'לוקה חמש' is a loose way of saying the person broke five prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לוקה' is not taken literally here. It only counts how many איסורים were broken, so the answer of Step 18 still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Five prohibitions

phrases.english: They are five prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 by reinterpreting רבא's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לוקה חמש' means five actual sets of מלקות.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means he violated five prohibitions.

steps.title: The משנה lists these people among those who get lashes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה of 'אלו הן הלוקין' lists a case that follows רבי שמעון, and it is a list of people who actually receive מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: 'These are the ones who are flogged'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer again, this time from the משנה itself. The answer to this challenge comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list includes a כהן who eats ביכורים before the קריאה, a case already explained as following רבי שמעון. A list titled 'these are the ones who are flogged' clearly means real מלקות, so 'just a prohibition' seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: 'These are the ones who are flogged': the opening of the משנה's list

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the משנה:
'These are the ones who are flogged'!
phrases.notes: The list includes a כהן who eats ביכורים before the קריאה. Earlier on the דף, that case was said to follow רבי שמעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן אֵלּוּ הֵן הַלּוֹקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the answers of Steps 18 and 20, this time from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון's derived prohibitions carry no מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה, which follows רבי שמעון, lists the ביכורים case among those who receive real lashes.
